paper.title_en: Chromatic photon-ring spectroscopy of asymmetric thin-shell wormholes in a dispersive plasma
paper.abstract_en: Wang et al. [Phys. Lett. B 811 (2020) 135930] proposed a distinctive shadow mechanism for asymmetric thin-shell wormholes (ATWs): a horizonless object may reproduce the exterior optical appearance of a Schwarzschild black hole while producing additional structures from rays that cross the throat and return from the second exterior. We study this mechanism for two unequal-mass Schwarzschild exteriors joined at a throat and immersed in cold, nonmagnetized, nonabsorbing plasma with <math altimg="si7.svg"><mrow><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><msubsup><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></mrow></math>. We derive the plasma-modified radial potential, critical impact parameters, shell-matched propagation window, and disk transfer functions. A central result of the revision is an exact scaling test. When <math altimg="si8.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si9.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math>, and both critical points are exterior maxima, <math altimg="si10.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>; hence the observer-side and projected opposite-side critical curves have identical fractional chromatic dependence. The equal-q model is therefore a self-similar control and does not by itself demonstrate differential ring motion. Genuine differential motion can occur when the two dimensionless plasma strengths or falloff indices differ. For equal plasma-frequency normalization coefficients, <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msub><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, shell energy matching implies <math altimg="si5.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></math>, and our fiducial example yields different normalized shifts of the main and extra critical scales. We present this as a conditional, plasma-model-dependent geometric diagnostic rather than a topology-only signature. The displayed intensity is a finite-order (m ≤ 4), independently normalized bolometric proxy for the transfer map, not an order-converged or self-consistent multifrequency radiative-transfer prediction.
